clarity_findings.claim: "Larger units" is unclear to a reader who knows nothing about ship units.
clarity_findings.problem: "A unit-size patent lets your shipyards build a ship in larger units." never says what a unit is. It also sits next to the "Ships" bullet without saying how the two differ. The brief says ships are plain text for now, but this reads as a placeholder.
clarity_findings.fix: Add a short clause that says what a unit is, for example "a unit merges several identical ships into one". If the term is not settled until the Ships chapter exists, say so in the guide map.

clarity_findings.claim: Three pointers say the same thing: "Each patent's page shows its ancestor...", "Each patent's own page lists exactly what it unlocks", and the intro's ownership line.
clarity_findings.problem: The catalog-page pointer appears in both The patent tree and What patents unlock, and "A patent is yours for the rest of the game" repeats "There is no refund". The repetition adds words without adding facts.
clarity_findings.fix: State the pointer to catalog pages once. Drop one of the two "yours for good" statements, for example keep the no-refund bullet and cut the intro sentence, or the reverse.

votes.reason: The page says each owned patent makes the next one dearer, but it gives no size or example of the increase and sends the "why" to another page. The table lists base prices only, so a player with a few patents can't tell what they will actually pay.
stumbles: "Every patent you own makes the next one dearer, and the panel's Cost Increase Factor shows by how much." There is no rate, formula or worked example, so the player has to open "How prices grow" to get the answer.

The table column "Base price" (for example "1,000" for Cookie-cutter Cities) is never tied to what the player pays now. It is unclear whether the price shown in the panel matches the table, or by how much it has drifted after a few purchases.

The page is about patents, so the player who has also bought a lex finds nothing on whether lexes affect patent prices or what they share with patents. The branch list ("Legacy and Tactic ... Flash") also names game modes with no explanation of which one the player is in.

votes.reason: The buy rules (need the ancestor, exact price is enough, instant, no refund) read in one pass; only the real price formula and the Flash patents are missing.
stumbles: "Every patent you own makes the next one dearer, and the panel's Cost Increase Factor shows by how much." The page gives no number or formula, so I can't work out what the next patent costs without following the price-scaling link. The table only lists "Base price".

"Flash: Economic, Military" is named as a branch set, but "All patents" shows only Legacy/Tactic branches (Origin, Habitable Planets, Barren Planets, Moons and Asteroids, Shipyards and Ships). A Flash player can't tell whether the table applies to them or where their patents are listed.

The Unlocks column mixes linked buildings with plain text, such as "2 Scouts", "Carrier", "Colonisation Ship" and "Allows for construction or merging of units of 4 Fighters". The ship names aren't linked, and "units of 4 Fighters" is only explained under "Larger units" as "build a ship in larger units", which doesn't say what a unit is.

Tied 'ancestor' to the catalog label and gave the catalog pointer only once, in The patent tree: "Each patent's page lists its ancestor under Requires, the path to it from {name:patent.citadel}, and exactly what it unlocks." Removed the duplicate "Each patent's own page lists exactly what it unlocks." from What patents unlock.

votes.reason: The page explains what patents are and how to buy them clearly, but it only hints at why prices rise and hands the actual explanation to another page, so I had to leave to learn what I came for.
stumbles: "Every patent you own makes the next one dearer, and the panel's Cost Increase Factor shows by how much. See How prices grow." gives no rate, formula or example, and the real answer is off-page.

"Each patent has a base price in technology, listed below, and its card shows the price you pay now." I can't tell how far the base prices in the table will drift from what I actually pay. Nothing says whether lexes or already-owned patents affect the rise.

The table lists a 50-technology patent next to a 150,000 one, and several later tiers cost less than earlier ones (Urbanization III at 2,000 comes after Maglev Architecture at 3,000). There is no note on whether to buy in order or by price, and no mention of lexes or how they relate to patent costs.

votes.reason: The buy rule, permanence, no-refund and click-to-buy behavior are stated cleanly, but the price growth is only a pointer and the table doesn't cover the Flash branches the page names.
stumbles: "Flash: Economic, Military" is listed as a branch, but the "All patents" table has only Origin, Habitable Planets, Barren Planets, Moons and Asteroids, and Shipyards and Ships rows. I can't tell whether Flash patents are missing from the table or share these rows, and whether the base prices apply to Flash.

"Every patent you own makes the next one dearer, and the panel's Cost Increase Factor shows by how much." Nothing here says how much. The exact rule is only behind "How prices grow", and the "Base price" column isn't what you pay.

The Unlocks column mixes styles. Some cells are bare "2 Scouts", "Carrier" or "Destroyer", while others are "Allows for construction or merging of units of 4 Fighters". The bare ship cells aren't linked, and "2 Scouts" reads as a quantity when the patent actually unlocks the ship type.
